Required findings: The individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.
Imaging findings include ANY of the following:
degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis with EITHER of the following:
dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image, with a difference in translational alignment between vertebrae >3mm between views
Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis
spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis (e.g., Isthmic Spondylolisthesis) with ANY of the following:
Meyerding Grade I or II spondylolisthesis (anterolisthesis) and plain x-rays support progression of anterolisthesis
Meyerding Grade III or higher spondylolisthesis (anterolisthesis) with ≥50% anterior slippage OR plain x-rays support progression of anterolisthesis
progressive spinal pain without confirmatory imaging showing progression of spondylolisthesis
multi-level spondylolysis on plain x-rays
post-operative instability created by the disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision that exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet
pars fracture
previous spinal decompression that resulted in iatrogenic spondylolisthesis
Criteria exception : When instability is created and/or identified intra-operatively, the above imaging criteria are NOT required.
Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following:
individual is a never-smoker

individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/ or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) > Actual Instability

Required findings: The individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.
Anticipated iatrogenic instability with ANY of the following:
created by disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet during spinal decompression
created by removal of the pars interarticularis that requires fusion to stabilize
created by decompression for Meyerding Grade I or higher spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis
created by complete or partial corpectomy (i.e., removal of at least one-third of the vertebral body [not for resection of osteophytes alone])
Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following:
individual is a never-smoker

individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/ or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

Required findings: The individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.
Imaging findings include EITHER of the following:
coronal plane deformity which includes ANY of the following:
Cobb angle >30°
asymmetric disk collapse causing symptomatic foraminal narrowing
global coronal imbalance causing head and trunk shift off the midline
sagittal imbalance which includes ANY of the following:
sagittal vertebral axis measurement >8cm
pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15°
Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following:
individual is a never-smoker

individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/ or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) > Adult Symptomatic Degenerative Spinal Deformity

Required findings: The individual is a candidate for an initial primary lumbar discectomy per the applicable section below:
For an initial primary lumbar discectomy, see CMM-606.2: Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) .
For information related to excision of extradural lesion other than neoplasm, see CMM 606.1: General Guidelines .
Advanced imaging shows ANY of the following:
primary extraforaminal disc herniation at L5-S1, in which a far lateral approach is not feasible because of the presence of the iliac wings
primary foraminal disc herniation for which facet resection is necessary to retrieve the disc, which will result in iatrogenic instability
primary disc herniation in the lumbar spine that is at the level of the spinal cord (i.e., low lying conus medullaris)
Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following:
individual is a never-smoker

individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/ or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) > Initial Disc Herniation

Required findings: The individual is a candidate for repeat lumbar discectomy per CMM 606.3: Repeat Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy or Laminectomy) at the Same Level .
Imaging findings include evidence of anterolisthesis at the requested level(s) that results in EITHER of the following:
dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image, with a difference in translational alignment between vertebrae >3mm between views
Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis
Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following:
individual is a never-smoker

individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/ or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

Non-Indications: The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the individual does not meet ALL of the associated criteria for the specific indication.
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if imaging findings do not support the diagnosis or instability criteria.
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if conservative management has not been adequately trialed and failed, as per policy requirements.
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the individual does not meet the qualifying rules (e.g., age restrictions, comorbidities).
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the individual has unmanaged behavioral or risk health disorders that could impact surgical outcomes or adherence to post-operative care.

The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the imaging findings do not show the specific structural abnormalities required for the indication (e.g., lack of spondylolisthesis, deformity, or disc herniation criteria).
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the patient has undergone a previous spinal fusion or decompression that did not meet the criteria.
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the patient has failed prior surgical interventions for the same condition.
The procedure is NOT medically necessary if the patient does not meet the nicotine-free status requirements.
Important criteria & exceptions: The individual must be a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.
Imaging findings are required to support the indication (e.g., instability, deformity, disc herniation).
Conservative management requirements must be met prior to considering surgery.
Nicotine-free status requirement must be met prior to surgery.
The specific imaging criteria for each indication must be met.
Intraoperative identification of instability may exempt the need for pre-operative imaging findings.
Documentation required: Imaging reports supporting the diagnosis and criteria (e.g., plain x-rays, CT scans, MRI scans showing spondylolisthesis, deformity, disc herniation, instability findings).
Therapy records demonstrating trial of conservative management.
Objective cotinine testing results confirming nicotine-free status within 6 weeks prior to surgery.
